testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does rust around wheel nuts mean?

options.text: It recently rained.
The nuts are loose.
The tires need to be replaced.
The nuts are too tight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts are loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts usually means they are loose. Check how tight the nuts are if you see rust in that area.

questions.question: Which person should NOT concern motorists as a distraction?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
A construction worker on the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful around people who are not paying attention to the road. Drivers and pedestrians talking to others may be distracted and not watching the road. Construction workers on the road may focus on their work instead of traffic, which can also distract drivers.

questions.question: What is a good rule to follow when making a turn?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Use your arms to get the attention of other drivers.
Turn off your turn signal before entering the turn to avoid confusing other drivers.
Signal early.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal early.
questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn so drivers behind you know your plans. Keep the signal on during the turn and turn it off after the turn is complete.

questions.question: Where should weight be placed when loading cargo?

options.text: As high as possible.
As low as possible.
As close to the cab as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Place cargo weight as low as possible to reduce the risk of the vehicle tipping over.

questions.question: How should cargo on flatbed trailers be secured?

options.text: Tied down.
Glued down.
Left loose.
Pushed to one side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tied down.
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down to prevent it from shifting or falling during transport.

questions.question: When driving, what areas should you watch?

options.text: Keep your attention in front of your vehicle.
Look only to the front and right side.
Look only to the front and sides.
Look to the front, sides, and rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the front, sides, and rear.
questions.explanation: To drive safely, you must be aware of everything around your vehicle. Watch the road ahead and use your mirrors often to check the sides and back of your vehicle.

questions.question: During interstate travel, which state's laws apply to cargo securement and vehicle weight?

options.text: The law of the state where the trip started.
The law of the state the vehicle is in.
The driver should ask for federal regulations to override state laws.
The driver can choose which state's laws to follow.

questions.correctAnswerText: The law of the state the vehicle is in.
questions.explanation: Vehicle weight, cargo securement, load covering, and where large vehicles can drive are controlled by federal, state, and local laws that vary by location. You must follow the laws of the state where you are driving.

questions.question: What should you check about belts during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Loosen them.
Check how tight they are.
Scrub them clean.
Do not inspect them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how tight they are.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, check all belts for proper tightness and excess wear. Learn how much movement is normal for each belt.

questions.question: After changing a tire, why should you stop after a short distance?

options.text: Check how tight the lug nuts are.
Make sure the tire stayed clean.
Inflate the new tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how tight the lug nuts are.
questions.explanation: After you change a tire, stop a short distance later to check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: What should you know about hearing trains at railroad crossings?

options.text: You will hear every approaching train.
You may not hear a train even if one is coming.
You will hear two short horn blasts if a train is approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hear a train even if one is coming.
questions.explanation: Never assume you will hear an approaching train. The train operator may not sound the horn, or horns may be prohibited in some areas. Even if the horn sounds, noise in your vehicle may prevent you from hearing the train until it is too close.

questions.question: When driving a heavy vehicle, how can you avoid interfering with traffic?

options.text: Switch gears while driving uphill.
Pass other vehicles while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane.
Use your brakes while driving downhill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle is too heavy to match the speed of other traffic, stay in the right lane when possible.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand.
With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
With both hands at the bottom of the wheel.
With both hands at the top of the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands placed on opposite sides.

questions.question: What will you be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?

options.text: Change a tire.
Explain what you would inspect and why.
Estimate the weight of a trailer load.
Change a windshield wiper.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you would inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your vehicle and explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.

questions.question: In an emergency stop, what should you do?

options.text: Veer your trailer right and stop.
Stop in a straight line.
Veer your trailer left and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop in a straight line.
questions.explanation: In an emergency, brake in a way that keeps your vehicle straight. You can use controlled braking or stab braking. Keep the vehicle straight but be ready to turn if needed.

questions.question: What is true about transporting livestock on a trailer?

options.text: Livestock should never be transported on a trailer.
A law enforcement officer must inspect the livestock.
Livestock can move and shift weight, causing unsafe handling.
Only registered farmers can transport livestock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Livestock can move and shift weight, causing unsafe handling.
questions.explanation: Livestock can move around and shift their weight while being transported. This can make the trailer unsafe to handle.

questions.question: How should manual air tank drains be used?

options.text: Open them to drain the tanks after each day.
Leave them open while driving.
Seal them with glue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open them to drain the tanks after each day.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems collect water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if left to build up. Open the manual drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Does talking on a hands-free phone while driving distract a driver?

options.text: No, it does not distract the driver.
Only if the driver is speaking.
Yes, it can distract the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it can distract the driver.
questions.explanation: Hands-free phones are safer than hand-held phones, but they still distract drivers. Talking on the phone takes your attention away from driving.

questions.question: What should you use to put out an electrical fire?

options.text: Water.
A B or C fire extinguisher.
An X fire extinguisher.
A Q fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: A B or C fire extinguisher.
questions.explanation: Use B or C type fire extinguishers for electrical fires. Never use water on electrical fires because it can cause electric shock.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air tank drains?

options.text: To allow rain water to enter air tanks.
To drain water and oil from air tanks.
They should never be opened.
They must remain open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: To drain water and oil from air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and compressor oil from the brake system. If these build up, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: If mirrors are dirty before you start driving, what should you do?

options.text: They will become clean after driving a short distance.
It is not a concern.
Clean them before you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clean them before you drive.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check your mirrors and windshield for dirt or anything blocking your view. Clean them before you start your trip.

questions.question: When putting out an electrical fire, you should:

options.text: Use water.
Use a B:C extinguisher.
Use an X extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a B:C extinguisher.
questions.explanation: B:C fire extinguishers work on electrical fires and burning liquids. Never use water on an electrical fire.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter a cab because of:

options.text: A defective exhaust system.
Using the wrong type of fuel.
A lack of oil in the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: A defective exhaust system.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is a serious safety problem. Poisonous fumes can leak into the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Reduce a vehicle's normal braking power.
Work with other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
Are not effective on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work with other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works with a vehicle's normal braking system. It does not increase or decrease braking power. ABS only activates when a vehicle's wheels are about to lock.

questions.question: Emergency brakes:

options.text: Are not required on trucks.
Are only required on trailers.
Are required on tractors.
Are optional.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required on tractors.
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must work by mechanical force.

questions.question: After an engine starts, the oil pressure should reach normal:

options.text: Within seconds.
Within five minutes.
Within three minutes.
After five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within seconds.
questions.explanation: When an engine starts, oil pressure should reach normal within seconds. Do not drive if oil pressure is too low.

questions.question: When traveling down a hill:

options.text: Your speed will not change.
Your speed will decrease.
Your speed will increase.
You will slow to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your speed will increase.
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls a vehicle down a slope, causing speed to increase.

questions.question: You should hold the steering wheel:

options.text: With both hands.
With one hand to keep the other hand free.
With one hand at a time, alternating between hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides.

questions.question: Carriers must keep fuel records for IFTA quarterly fuel tax returns for:

options.text: One year.
Two years.
Three years.
Four years.

questions.correctAnswerText: Four years.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles operating interstate must register under the International Registration Plan (IRP) and International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA). Carriers must keep mileage and fuel records for IFTA quarterly fuel tax returns for four years.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks need special care because:

options.text: They have low centers of gravity.
They have high centers of gravity.
Loads are usually stable.
They are usually overloaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity and loads often shift during travel. Be extra careful when turning and taking curves.

questions.question: Scan the road ____ ahead of your vehicle.

options.text: Two to three seconds
Five to six seconds
12 to 15 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: 12 to 15 seconds
questions.explanation: Good drivers scan the road at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This helps you see and react to hazards before you reach them. Look for vehicles entering the highway, changing lanes, or turning.

questions.question: When driving in wet conditions, if you see no spray coming from other vehicles' tires, what does this mean?

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The pavement is dry.
The spray is stuck under the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: When driving in wet conditions, no spray from other vehicles' tires means ice is on the road. Be extra careful when driving in wet weather that is also cold.

questions.question: On a CDL vehicle inspection test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Check the engine oil level.
Replace a tire.
Remove the alternator belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the engine oil level.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will check the engine oil level in the engine compartment.

questions.question: For a vehicle with air brakes, what condition should the air compressor drive belt be in before each drive?

options.text: Loose
Tight
Cracked
Bumpy

questions.correctAnswerText: Tight
questions.explanation: Before each drive, check the air compressor belt on air brake vehicles. The belt should be tight and in good condition.

questions.question: When inspecting the engine compartment, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check the engine oil level.
Check the coolant level in the radiator.
Drain the brake fluid.
Check the windshield washer fluid level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drain the brake fluid.
questions.explanation: During engine compartment inspection, check the oil level, coolant level, and windshield washer fluid level. Do not drain the brake fluid.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Change a tire.
Explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.
Estimate the weight of cargo on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will do a complete inspection. You must explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Move quickly to stay out of other drivers' way.
Try not to use the mirrors.
Use a helper if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a helper if possible.
questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Use a helper whenever you can to watch your blind spots.

questions.question: During a trip, gauges are:

options.text: Often misleading.
The only way a driver can learn of vehicle problems.
One way to learn of vehicle problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: One way to learn of vehicle problems.
questions.explanation: During a trip, regularly check the gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights for signs of trouble.

questions.question: Header boards:

options.text: Should never be used.
Protect the driver from cargo hitting them.
Protect the driver's head when entering the truck cab.
Provide extra storage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo hitting them.
questions.explanation: Header boards (also called "headache racks") protect the driver from cargo that shifts during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: If you feel tired and keep yawning, you should:

options.text: Keep driving.
Get some coffee.
Drive faster.
Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: Frequent yawning means you are tired. The only safe thing to do is stop and sleep. Coffee and other stimulants will wear off and make you more tired later.

questions.question: When traveling with cargo, when should the cargo be checked?

options.text: Only before the trip.
Before the trip and after the first 50 miles.
Only by loading personnel.
Only after arriving at the final destination.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip and after the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before the trip starts, after the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or every 150 miles. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safely secured the entire trip.

questions.question: Air tanks usually hold enough compressed air:

options.text: For one stop before needing to be refilled.
For several stops before needing to be refilled.
For a day's worth of braking.
For an unlimited number of stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: For several stops before needing to be refilled.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold enough compressed air for the brakes to work several times before needing to be refilled.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:

options.text: Attitude.
How quickly you arrive at your destination.
Your general driving behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your general driving behavior.
questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on specific driving skills and your overall driving behavior during the test.

questions.question: To work on a vehicle, ABS:

options.text: Must be on all axles.
Must be on the rear axle.
Can be on as few as one axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be on as few as one axle.
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes on just one axle still give the driver better control while braking than having no anti-lock brakes at all.

questions.question: Blocking a load:

options.text: Is only done with liquid cargo.
Helps to stabilize the load.
Is dangerous and should never be done.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps to stabilize the load.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing prevent cargo from shifting during transport.

questions.question: When making a tight turn, a CMV operator should:

options.text: Be able to drive as fast as a car.
Not worry about speed, but focus on the road.
Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind.
questions.explanation: Drivers behind you may not expect your CMV to slow down for a turn. Brake early and slow down gradually to warn them in advance.

questions.question: When doing a pre-drive inspection:

options.text: The inspection report is not important.
The inspection report must only be reviewed if there will be passengers in the vehicle.
Review the previous inspection report, if there is one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Review the previous inspection report, if there is one.
questions.explanation: The first step is to review the last vehicle inspection report. Only sign the report if any listed problems have been fixed.

questions.question: The parking brake should be:

options.text: Used whenever you park the vehicle.
Used while driving.
Set when driving in bad weather.
Used to stop the vehicle during normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Used whenever you park the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Apply the parking brake every time you park your vehicle.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Is a good way to stay awake on long trips.
Is distracting.
Can cause mechanical damage.
Should be used to prevent rust from forming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause mechanical damage.
questions.explanation: Always accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can damage your vehicle's engine and parts.

questions.question: Rims with welding repairs:

options.text: Are not safe to be used.
Are acceptable to be used on the rear tires of a vehicle.
Are acceptable to be used only when carrying a heavy load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not safe to be used.
questions.explanation: Never use wheels or rims that have been repaired by welding.

questions.question: After a vehicle is started, warning lights and buzzers:

options.text: Should stay on for several minutes.
Should turn off within a few seconds.
Should stay on until manually turned off.
Should remain on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should go off right after starting the engine. If a light stays on, your vehicle may have a problem.
